resources.string: Choose one backend and request its permission. Configuration, saving and module generation become available only after a permission is granted; installing the APK alone does not execute anything.
No module flashed: mount groups are not restored automatically after a reboot.
The target app is force-stopped and its data directory is cleared; the configuration is kept and other groups are unaffected.

An app version no longer matches the value recorded when this share was created. Mounts were unmounted and the target side was cleared by this group path list; the configuration is kept. With optional background checking this can also happen while the app is closed. Finish updating resources in the primary app first, then tap Re-share; do not open the target app before that, or it may re-download.

Have you finished updating resources in the primary app? Re-share force-stops the target app, clears its data directory, then re-mounts the same directories and completes the loose files. Other groups are unaffected. The result is confirmed by reading as the target app.
This update did not change shared resources; restore from current data anyway
Re-shared with the original configuration; the current version is now the new baseline.
Rebuilt from the primary app’s current data; the current version is now the new baseline.
Copied again from the primary app’s current data.
The target side has been cleared. Retry, or let the target app re-download. Configuration is kept.
Pause only unmounts and keeps every file and setting; Resume re-mounts as-is. Hard links and copy are on-disk state with no pause action.
Module generated, flash it to finish

For mount groups only. Flash it to restore mounts automatically at boot; without it, open this app after each reboot to re-apply. Hard links and copies are already on disk and need neither the module nor this step.

The zip is saved to Download/AndroidDataShare/. Install it from local storage in Magisk / KernelSU / APatch; no immediate reboot is needed, it applies at the next boot. Version checking still runs in this app.
Module generation failed; the button stays available. Check the error and retry.
Existing mount groups may stop working after this switch
Changing the method revokes the old share first
Changing the method revokes the old share first so two methods never run at once. You will be asked to pick the new method next; the revocation happens when you save.
Module flashed: mounts are restored automatically at boot.
%1$s rule(s) did not take effect; check the execution log.

A recoverable copy of hard-link groups was found on this device (user 0 Download/AndroidDataShare/linkstate.json). It contains configuration and version baselines only, no account data. After restoring, each group is compared with its recorded version: it is marked Rebuild pending only when the primary app version actually changed. No files are deleted or rebuilt automatically. Check the group list afterwards.
Keep the record, do not restore
A record that does not belong to this app was ignored.
Let multiple clients of the same game share one set of static assets. Pick a primary app and a target app, then share data via hard link, copy, or mount.
Support is voluntary and does not purchase software, features or services, and does not affect any functionality.
Target side cleared; configuration is kept. Tap the right action to replay it when ready.
The target app is force-stopped, mounts are removed, and its data directory is cleared. The configuration is kept, so Re-share can replay it later.
Share terminated and the target side cleared; configuration is kept.

A version change was detected: the mount was removed, the fill-ins and the target side were cleared, and the configuration is kept. Finish updating resources in the primary app, then tap Re-share. You can also ignore this: the target app simply re-downloads its own resources.

Notice only: nothing was terminated and no file was cleared. The primary app version changed; finish its resource update before optionally tapping Rebuild links. A target-only update does not trigger this notice; do not rebuild in that case, or the primary app current data will overwrite the target. You can also ignore this.
Check that both clients update in sync first

This feature suits different servers of one game whose resource version and update schedule stay in sync. If the two sides update on different schedules, sharing may cause repeated re-downloads, asset verification failures or crashes. Hard links, copy and mount all share the same current data; none of them aligns versions, and switching method does not fix it. For such games, let each side download and update on its own and do not create a share.
Do not show this kind of notice again
These two clients are known to update out of sync

Known: %1$s and %2$s do not stay in sync on updates. Sharing may cause repeated re-downloads, asset verification failures or crashes. Hard links, copy and mount all share the same current data; none aligns versions, and switching method does not fix it. It is best not to create this share and let each side download and update on its own.

The target is in a different user from the primary app. A cross-user mount may not take effect: even if the command succeeds, the target app may be unable to read it because each user has an independent storage view. Whether it works is confirmed by reading as the target app.

Once Mount is working, files added, deleted or replaced inside the directory are followed automatically. If the app cannot see them, check whether your root setup offers a global mount namespace option. If that does not help, try Hard link or Copy instead.

Once working, added, deleted or replaced files are followed automatically, with no completion and no rebuild. Bind mounting works only on some systems: it may be mounted yet unreadable. Whether it works is confirmed by reading as the target app. This scope is exclusive with other groups for the same target.
Mounted files follow automatically; loose files at the package root need to be filled in separately.

After the primary app updates, tap Re-share to rebuild. Stopping removes these items; restoring rebuilds them from the primary app’s current data, so anything the target app wrote meanwhile is not kept.
Hard link: no extra space. Copy: a separate snapshot that takes extra space. Neither follows later updates to the primary app; tap Re-share to rebuild.
Grant an execution permission first. Creating, editing or saving groups and generating the module are disabled until then, so nothing is configured without being able to run.
Configuration restored. Grant permission to save and apply changes; the module button appears only after permission is granted.
Permission was not granted. Check Shizuku / Sui or your root manager, then try again.

Shizuku (non-root) normally lacks the privilege required to mount, so existing mount groups may stop working after the switch. This group keeps its current execution channel; the permission state was still recorded. Whether to switch share method is up to you.

By default only the APK version is checked. Some games update resources without changing the APK version, so no change would be detected. If you know a file inside Android/data that changes with each resource update (for example files/version.txt), enter its relative path here; its checksum is added to the version baseline. Leave it empty to keep the default behaviour.
No running Shizuku / Sui service was found. Start Shizuku, or install and enable Sui, then try again.
Whole package directory: every file follows automatically, no scattered files need completing and no rebuild is needed.
This method handles the whole package directory; no directory scan is needed.

Both sides look like real files taking up space, but they point to the same data and use only one copy of storage; the two directory entries are equal, with no primary side. After the primary app updates, tap Rebuild links to save space again, or just keep using it.

Once working, added, deleted or replaced files inside the mounted directory are followed automatically. Success is confirmed by reading as the target app; if it cannot see them, check whether your root setup offers a global mount namespace option. If that does not help, try Hard link or Copy instead.

Fallback only: keeps a second full copy and uses extra space. Use it only when hard links and mount both fail and you do not want the target app to download resources again. The two sides are independent and do not follow updates.
The commands being executed scroll below; large directories may take a while.
Current state: Rebuild pending (primary app updated)
Current state: Target updated on its own (no rebuild)

When enabled, this app compares version baselines in the background: a hard-link change only posts a notification, a mount change terminates the share and notifies you. When disabled, checks run only after opening the app. Vendor auto-start switches must be set manually.

The authorised Shizuku / Sui / Root backend will silently set standard OS items (battery whitelist, background app-op, standby bucket). No system dialog, never on by default, reversible here at any time. Vendor auto-start switches still need the settings page. A whitelist does not guarantee the process is never killed; declining changes nothing.
Standard background items are reset and the foreground service stops. If you enabled a vendor auto-start switch manually, turn it off in the settings page yourself.
Some OS items could not be set; background checks may be less timely. Opening the app still checks.
A hard-link group has a primary-side version change. After the primary finishes updating, Rebuild links only merges the data back to save space again; doing nothing is fine.
A version change was detected: the mount was removed and its fill-ins cleared. Finish updating resources in the primary app, then tap Re-share.
A hard-link group is pending rebuild and a mount group was terminated. Open the app for details.
Comparing shared groups against their recorded version baselines.
Cross-user mount may not take effect
Creating a group first clears the data directory of the target app, then establishes the share using %1$s.
Saving force-stops the target app first, then updates this group by the changes made; existing data in the target app is not cleared. The configuration is kept and other groups are unaffected.
The target is the same app in the same user as the primary, so it would share data with itself. Pick another client or switch to a different user.
This app in this user is already used in another group, as primary or target, or is duplicated inside this group. One data set can belong to only one group; add targets in the existing group instead.
App already belongs to another group
This app is already used in another group, as its primary or a target, so it cannot be the primary of a new group. To share with more clients, edit that group and add targets there.
Also clear the target app’s directory
Delete "%1$s"? The target app’s directory will be cleared as well.
This backend may not be able to finish sharing

Shizuku-only runs as the shell user. It cannot reach app data under /data/media/USER/, so this app retries via the public storage path of the primary user. Only Copy usually works there: the public storage view supports neither hard links nor mounts, and users other than 0 are out of reach. Switch back to Copy, or use root / Sui. Failures are listed one by one.
Done. The full output is saved to Download/AndroidDataShare/run.log. Open it in a file manager; each run overwrites it, so only the latest is kept.
Pick folders or individual files; a picked folder is expanded into its files when applied.
This system seems to block or restrict hard links; Copy mode may be the only option.
This stops the run and clears everything already created in the target directory. This cannot be undone.
Stopped. Anything already created in the target directory has been cleared.
Could not send the pause or resume command; the run may keep going.
